rotor_tip_speed_CR.quote: Rotor tip speed (based on casing radius) 61.15 m / s

max_speed.quote: The compressor will accommodate rotational speeds to 1050 rpm and is rated at a pressure ratio of 1.042.

mass_flow.quote: Mass flow ... 12.3 kg/sec (TM Table I); Mass flow 12.3 kg / s (CR Table III.1, PDF p. 29)

axial_velocity.quote: Axial velocity ... 24.4 m/sec (CR Table III.1: 24.4 m /s)

pressure_ratio.quote: Pressure ratio ... 1.042 (same in CR Table III.1)

temperature_ratio.quote: Temperature ratio ... 1.013 (same in CR Table III.1)

flow_coefficient_definition.quote: These are all given with respect to flow coefficient, defined as the mean inlet velocity normalized by the tip speed.

stage_count.quote: The low-speed axial compressor consists of four repeating stages (i.e., rotor and stator blade rows) plus an inlet guide vane (IGV) row, as shown in figure 3.

repeating_stages_CR.value: identical blade geometry in all four stages; stage 3 is the test stage
repeating_stages_CR.quote: Four repeating stages (stages with identical blade geometry) were used. The first two stages were assumed to set up a repeating stage environment. The third stage was considered the test stage.

blade_count_stator_and_igv.quote: Number of blades Stator and IGV 52 (both reports)

rotor_aspect_ratio_constant.quote: The aspect ratios for each blade were kept constant along the span (AR ≈ 1.2).

midspan_chord_rotor.quote: Aerodynamic chord midspan Rotor ... 10.2 cm (both reports)

midspan_chord_stator.quote: Aerodynamic chord midspan Stator ... 9.4 cm (both reports)

midspan_axial_chord_rotor.quote: Axially projected chord midspan Rotor ... 7.6 cm

midspan_axial_chord_stator.quote: Axially projected chord midspan Stator ... 6.6 cm

midspan_setting_angle_rotor.quote: Blade setting angle midspan Rotor ... 43° (both reports)

midspan_setting_angle_stator.quote: Blade setting angle midspan Stator ... 42° (both reports)

axial_gap.quote: Axial gap between blade rows ... 2.54 cm (TM); Nominal axial gap 2.54 cm (CR, PDF p. 29)

stator_seal_clearance_CR.quote: Stator shroud labyrinth seal 0.85 mm (0.70% span)

seal_clearance_measurement.value: static, 12 and 6 o'clock, normalized by span 12.19 cm
seal_clearance_measurement.quote: For both sets of experiments, seal-tooth clearances were measured statically at the 12 and 6 o'clock positions before and after each configuration change. ... The values are nondimensionalized by the blade span (12.19 cm) for convenience.

seal_clearance_nominal_definition.quote: To obtain mean values, averages were taken for all four stages. These averages are represented by the nominal values given in TableV.1.

baseline_leakage_rate.quote: The baseline configuration produced a leakage rate (nominally 0.45% of the power stream massflow) which could be found in aircraft core compressors utilizing current sealing technology [18].

stator_shroud_and_seal.value: shrouded stators, one labyrinth seal-tooth, blade ends sealed
stator_shroud_and_seal.quote: For each of the stages, the stators were shrouded with one labyrinth seal-tooth in the shrouded stator cavity and were sealed at both the hub and case blade tip interfaces.

stator_footring_TM.quote: (5) All four stator rows are shrouded on the hub end by insertion into a stator footring. Figure 6 shows the details of the stator footrings with a single labyrinth seal.

rotor1_casing_treatment.quote: (1) Circumferential grooves were provided in the casing wall over the tip of the first stage rotor (fig. 3).

blading_origin_CR.value: GE Rotor B / Stator B (Contract NAS3-20070; Wisler [15] = NASA CR 135391), modified for the different hub-to-tip ratio
blading_origin_CR.quote: The blading used for all tests were based on the Rotor B / Stator B geometry designed by General Electric, under Contract NAS3-20070, and tested in their Low-Speed Research Compressor. ... Complete details of the original designs were given by Wisler [15]. Some simple modifications to original geometry were incorporated into the NASA blades because of the differences in the hub-to-tip ratios of the two facilities.

blading_origin_TM.value: machine modeled after GE 1950s low-speed research compressor; blading after the E3-support model of the early 1980s
blading_origin_TM.quote: The NASA compressor was modeled after a low-speed research compressor developed by the General Electric Co. during the 1950's. The blading, however, was designed after the model used in support of a program to develop energy efficient engines in the early 1980's.

direct_scale_of_GE.quote: Since the NASA compressor was designed as a direct scale of the General Electric machine, tip treatment over the first rotor was also incorporated in the NASA design.

rotor_angle_modification.value: NASA rotor angles match GE at hub, not at tip
rotor_angle_modification.quote: NASA's angles match GE's angles at the hub, but not at the tip. This departure from the original design was incorporated in order to account for the different hub-to-tip ratios and attempted to keep velocity triangles the same across the span between the two geometries.

rotor_profile.value: modified circular-arc meanline, 2 deg LE and 6 deg TE overcambering; modified circular-arc thickness
rotor_profile.quote: The rotor consisted of airfoil sections having modified circular-arc meanlines with 2° and 6° overcambering at the leading and trailing edges. The stacking axis was at 50% chord. Modified circular-arc thickness distributions were used.

rotor_stacking.quote: The stacking axis was at 50% chord.

rotor_max_thickness_location.value: 60% chord at tip, blending to 50% chord at pitchline
rotor_max_thickness_location.quote: At the tip maximum thickness was at 60% chord. This blended to 50% chord at the pitchline.

stator_profile.value: 65-series thickness on modified circular-arc meanline, 3.5 deg LE overcambering, no TE overcambering, end-bends at hub and case
stator_profile.quote: As seen, the stators employ end-bends at both the hub and case. ... The stator consisted of airfoil sections having 65-series thickness distributions on a modified circular-arc meanline. Leading edge overcambering (3.5°) was needed in order to achieve representative suction surface velocity distributions. No trailing edge overcambering was incorporated.

stator_stacking.quote: In order to prevent this, the airfoil sections were stacked at the 30% chord location, instead of the usual 50%.

stator_twist_modification.value: linear twist hub to tip, tip angles increased by about 1.2
stator_twist_modification.quote: As with the rotor, to keep the velocity triangle distributions the same across the span, NASA's geometry employed a linear twist from hub to tip which increased the tip angles by about 1.2°.

stator_aspect_ratio_solidity.value: AR matched to GE, solidity allowed to vary
stator_aspect_ratio_solidity.quote: Aspect ratio distributions were matched while solidity distributions were allowed to vary.

spanwise_convention.quote: the spanwise variations, presented as percent span from the hub, of both NASA's and GE's blading parameters are presented.

measurement_stations_TM.quote: Figure 3.—Low-speed axial compressor aerodynamic survey locations. (legend A-L; D = Rotor 1 (Tip treatment))

measurement_stations_CR.quote: Data was taken at the rotor inlet, stator inlet and stator discharge for the third stage. These locations correspond to Stations 3.0, 3.5 and 4.0 respectively as shown in Figure III.1.

variable_stagger.value: all rows adjustable before a run
variable_stagger.quote: (3) All blade rows in the compressor have the option of variable stagger (i.e., blade setting angle) adjustment, and can be adjusted prior to a research run.

angle_convention.quote: (not stated in either report; CR nomenclature only lists the symbol as 'Blade setting angle')
